title: Host Paging Hysteresis and PCIe Throttling Playbook for KV Offload
content:
Purpose
This playbook defines a conservative, observable strategy for offloading KV cache pages from GPU-local memory to host CPU memory (or host-backed swap) and for applying adaptive PCIe bandwidth throttling when host residency pressure or I/O contention threatens latency SLOs. It is intended as an operational-ready spec that engineers can implement in the serving runtime and iterate on via experiments.

Background and motivation
We operate in mixed hardware environments: UMA (integrated) nodes and discrete-GPU nodes across cloud providers and private deployments. To keep token-level latency predictable under heavy context windows and multi-tenant workloads, we need a robust host-paging policy for the KV cache with:
- Clear thresholds that avoid oscillation between resident and offloaded states.
- A throttling mechanism to protect tail latency when PCIe or host I/O is saturated.
- Metrics and fail-safe behaviors for graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model variant, aggressive eviction, and per-customer rate-limiting).

Design goals
- Keep steady-state latency within SLOs for 99th percentile requests.
- Minimize unnecessary PCIe transfers that increase cost and tail latency.
- Avoid frequent churn of hot KV entries (avoid ping-pong).
- Provide observability hooks (events, traces, per-route stats).
- Be conservative by default; permit aggressive modes under controlled experiments.

Constraints and assumptions
- HW: PCIe gen3/4 links, NVMe host storage used only as last resort; primary offload target is host DRAM. UMA nodes expose lower-latency host access.
- Workloads: mixture of short chat sessions and long-context generation (up to 128k tokens per request in some workloads).
- Runtime: continuous batching, KV cache keyed by model-version + session, supports partial KV materialization.

Key concepts and terminology
- Residency: percentage of an active model's KV size that is resident on GPU.
- Offload threshold: residency level below which pages start being proactively migrated out to host memory.
- Fill threshold: residency level above which we stop pre-emptive offloads and begin refetching on-demand.
- Hysteresis window: gap between offload and fill thresholds to avoid oscillation.
- Throttling budget: a moving-window limit on PCIe bandwidth consumption we allow for KV transfers.

High-level approach
1) Track per-device and per-model residency percentages and a short-term trend (5s EWMA) for page churn.
2) When GPU free memory drops below a high-water mark, enter a conservative offload mode that throttles background transfers and only offloads cold pages.
3) If free memory continues falling despite conservative mode, escalate to emergency eviction where hotter pages may be migrated and prefetching is disabled.
4) Apply a PCIe throttling controller that enforces a bandwidth cap per-second and deprioritizes background transfers relative to foreground requests.
5) Log every transition with trace IDs and include metrics for prefetch vs on-demand transfer ratios.

Hysteresis algorithm (pseudocode)
- Definitions: free_mem_pct = (free_gpu_mem / total_gpu_mem) * 100
- thresholds: offload_trigger = 22% ; fill_resume = 35% (example defaults for discrete-GPU nodes)
- hysteresis_gap = fill_resume - offload_trigger = 13%
- state machine:
  state = RESIDENT_HEALTHY | CONSERVATIVE_OFFLOAD | EMERGENCY_EVICT
  on memory_check():
    if state == RESIDENT_HEALTHY and free_mem_pct <= offload_trigger:
      transition -> CONSERVATIVE_OFFLOAD
      schedule background cold-page offloads (rate-limited)
    elif state == CONSERVATIVE_OFFLOAD and free_mem_pct >= fill_resume:
      transition -> RESIDENT_HEALTHY
      stop background offloads
    elif free_mem_pct <= emergency_floor (e.g., 8%):
      transition -> EMERGENCY_EVICT
      perform aggressive eviction and disable prefetch/prefault
    elif state == EMERGENCY_EVICT and free_mem_pct >= emergency_recover (e.g., 18%):
      transition -> CONSERVATIVE_OFFLOAD

Rationale for concrete defaults
- offload_trigger around low-20s % keeps a reasonable batch of free pages to satisfy ephemeral kernel allocations and avoids immediate out-of-memory.
- fill_resume significantly higher to prevent flip-flop when workloads have bursts.
- emergency_floor must be low enough to avoid premature aggressive evictions but high enough to keep kernel allocations succeeding.
These defaults are starting points; experimentation table below recommends tuning by instance size and model footprint.

PCIe throttling controller
We propose a token-bucket style controller per-GPU that controls non-critical KV transfer bandwidth. Foreground requests that block generation must be admitted with priority; background paging and prefetch transfers must consume tokens and be rate-limited.
Parameters:
- bucket_rate (bytes/sec): baseline allowed bandwidth for background transfers (e.g., 4 GiB/s on high-end hosts, 1 GiB/s on smaller instances).
- bucket_capacity (bytes): short burst allowance (e.g., 1.5 * bucket_rate).
- priority_factor: multiplier to deprioritize background transfers (0.2–0.5).
- foreground_safety_margin: a small reserve (e.g., 10%) of PCIe bandwidth always kept for synchronous pulls.

Behavior:
- Background transfer is only allowed when bucket has tokens. When bucket is empty, background tasks are paused.
- Foreground transfers siphon tokens from a separate fast-path buffer but will trigger emergency eviction if they cause host memory exhaustion.
- If overall system I/O latency (measured at kernel level or via nvlink/pcie counters) rises above threshold, reduce bucket_rate by 50% and raise offload_trigger by +5% to avoid further pressure.

Page selection and coldness heuristics
- Use a multi-factor coldness score: last_access_age (ms), ref_count, size_in_pages, session_priority, sticky_flag (pinned pages).
- Cold score = w1*age + w2*(1/ref_count) + w3*size_norm - w4*pinned_flag.
- Evict highest cold score first for background offloads.
- Hot pages touched within last X ms (configurable) are protected from background eviction.

Prefetch & prewarming policy
- Disable aggressive prefetch when in CONSERVATIVE_OFFLOAD or EMERGENCY_EVICT state.
- Warm-up prefetch permitted during RESIDENT_HEALTHY and when background token bucket has healthy fill.
- Prefetch budget: max_prefetch_per_minute per model-version per device to limit runaway traffic from new large contexts.

UMA vs discrete fallback rules
- UMA: lower hysteresis_gap and lower offload_trigger because host access latency is smaller; prefer on-demand fetch rather than background offload.
- Discrete: prefer background offload earlier but with stronger throttling due to higher PCIe cost.

Metrics to collect (per-device, per-model, per-route)
- free_mem_pct, resident_pct, background_transfer_bytes/sec, foreground_transfer_bytes/sec
- prefetch_count, prefetch_hit_rate, on_demand_fetch_count, fetch_latency_p50/p95/p99
- eviction_count, re-fetch_rate (number of evicted pages re-fetched within T window)
- pci_bandwidth_utilization, pci_latency_ms, host_mem_pressure_events
- transitions of state machine and timestamps (for postmortem)

Experimentation plan and benchmarks
- Controlled benchmark matrix across instance types (g4dn, p4d-like private images, UMA dev boxes) and model sizes (7B, 34B, 70B).
- For each combination run: steady-state chat mix, spike mix (simultaneous 100 short bursts), and single large-context tail-case (1 request 100k tokens build-up).
- Measure 99th and 99.9th latency, cost of PCIe egress (if billable), and re-fetch rate.
- Iteration targets: re-fetch_rate < 0.5% for steady-state, p99 latency regression < 5% vs baseline.

Rollout plan and safety knobs
- Implement runtime flags to control thresholds and controller toggles per-cluster.
- Release behind a feature flag and run canary on non-critical clusters for 2 weeks.
- Add automated rollback if p99 latency or error rate increases above small thresholds.
- Safety config: if host_mem_pressure_events exceed N in M minutes, automatically reduce per-route concurrency for impacted tenants.

Operational runbook snippets
- Symptom: p99 latency increases and pci_bandwidth_utilization is near 100%
  - Check state transitions for GPUs in the cluster. If in CONSERVATIVE_OFFLOAD, temporarily reduce background bucket_rate to 25%.
  - Temporarily pin high-priority tenant models to resident-only mode (no offload) until pressure subsides.
- Symptom: high re-fetch_rate after eviction
  - Increase hysteresis gap (raise fill_resume by +8%).
  - Lower aggressiveness of cold-score weights for size_in_pages.

Open questions and tradeoffs
- Exact numeric defaults depend heavily on instance class and model shape — how do we automate per-instance tuning? (ML-driven controller?)
- Should we expose per-customer quotas on background paging budget to prevent noisy neighbors? (pro: isolation; con: complexity)
- How to reconcile cloud provider billing for PCIe egress (if applicable) with cost attribution in our chargeback model?

Action items
- Implementation: Diego to prototype token-bucket controller and state machine (PR linked).
- Benchmarks: Lina to run cross-instance matrix and populate canonical tuning table by 2024-09-01.
- Observability: Omar to add tracing labels to state transitions and wire up dashboard tiles.
- Follow-up: schedule a post-canary retro to decide defaults and opt-in flags.

Appendix: quick reference defaults (starting point)
- discrete GPUs: offload_trigger=22% ; fill_resume=35% ; emergency_floor=8% ; bucket_rate=4 GiB/s ; bucket_capacity=6 GiB
- UMA nodes: offload_trigger=15% ; fill_resume=24% ; emergency_floor=6% ; bucket_rate=1.2 GiB/s ; bucket_capacity=2 GiB
- re-fetch penalty tolerance: re-fetch_rate_target < 1% for aggressive workloads

End of playbook

Notes: This doc intentionally focuses on operational and parameterized behavior rather than microkernel implementation details. Implementation should emit rich telemetry and support rapid tuning via feature flags and per-cluster overrides.
